summary:
ANDEAN CLIMATE DETECTIVE is a 3D web game and data explorer that lets anyone check, with NASA data, whether the climate of the upper Santa River basin (Cordillera Blanca, Peru) is really changing. Players walk the valley with Inti, the river’s guardian, and visit five stations: temperature, rain, snow, groundwater, and stormwater. At each one they predict whether the variable rose, fell, or stayed the same, then see what the data shows and how certain it is.

Behind every answer is a reproducible statistical test. We remove seasonality and apply the Mann-Kendall trend test and Sen’s slope to MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, GLDAS, and MODIS data. We then cross-check the results with independent datasets (ERA5 and CHIRPS). The result: warming is confirmed by two sources (+0.2 to +0.3 °C per decade), and groundwater feeding the river in the dry season is declining. Rainfall shows no consistent trend, and snow loss appears at the glacier edge near Nevado Pastoruri.

This matters because over a million people rely on this basin’s water. Our tool turns satellite data into clear, honest answers, including what the data cannot yet prove.
details:
What it does
ANDEAN CLIMATE DETECTIVE answers one question for the upper Santa River basin (Cordillera Blanca, Peru): is the local climate really changing, or does it just feel that way?

  • 3D web game. Players explore the valley with Inti, the river’s guardian, and visit five stations: temperature, rain, snow, groundwater, and stormwater. At each station they first predict whether the variable rose, fell, or stayed the same. Then they “uncover the clue”: the observed change, a certainty level from 1 to 5, and a stamp that reads CONFIRMED, EVIDENCE (indicio), or NO PROOF. At the end, a time machine shows how far the snowline rises with the measured warming.
  • Data explorer. For each variable it shows the full monthly series with zoom, date search, seasonal or anomaly views, a data table, CSV download, and a link to reproduce the data in NASA Giovanni or AppEEARS.

How it works

  1. We downloaded monthly area-averaged series for the basin from NASA Giovanni:
    • MERRA-2 temperature (1981–2025)
    • GPM IMERG precipitation
    • GLDAS 2.1 surface runoff and groundwater runoff (2000–2025)
  2. We downloaded MODIS snow cover and land surface temperature for six Cordillera Blanca points from AppEEARS.
  3. A Python pipeline removes the seasonal cycle and applies the Mann-Kendall trend test with Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction, plus Sen’s slope with 95 % confidence intervals.
  4. When a trend is not significant, the pipeline estimates how many more years of data would be needed to detect it (Weatherhead et al., 1998).
  5. We validated each result against independent datasets from the KNMI Climate Explorer: ERA5 temperature and precipitation, CHIRPS precipitation, and the Niño 3.4 index. A trend counts as “confirmed” only if at least two sources agree.
  6. The results are compiled into a single data file that powers both the game and the explorer.

Key findings

  • Warming is confirmed by two sources: +0.28 °C per decade in MERRA-2 and +0.20 °C per decade in ERA5.
  • Groundwater feeding the river in the dry season declines about 16 % per decade.
  • Precipitation shows no consistent trend: the three sources disagree.
  • Dry-season snow is shrinking at the glacier edge near Nevado Pastoruri. This is evidence from a single point, not proof.

Benefits and intended impact
Farmers, communities, local authorities, and students can check climate claims about their own valley with real data, without needing to know statistics. The tool separates real trends from year-to-year noise and El Niño events, and it states openly what the data cannot yet prove. The design is not tied to the Santa basin: any region can be loaded by downloading the same Giovanni and AppEEARS series and running one script.

Tools and technologies

  • Analysis: Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, pyMannKendall, Matplotlib).
  • Game and explorer: JavaScript, HTML, and CSS with Three.js. There is no build step, and the app runs offline in any browser.
  • Earlier prototype: Streamlit.
  • Data tools: NASA Giovanni, NASA AppEEARS, and KNMI Climate Explorer.
  • Other: Git and GitHub. Claude (Anthropic) assisted with code and documentation (see our AI disclosure). No special hardware is needed.

What makes it creative

  • Instead of a dashboard, it is a detective story in which the player predicts before seeing the data. This turns statistical significance into something people can feel.
  • The verdict stamps (Confirmed, Evidence, No proof) teach that “different” is not the same as “a trend”.
  • The guardian Inti and the Andean valley root the experience in local culture.

Factors we considered

  • Statistical validity:
    • We used autocorrelation-corrected tests.
    • We did not merge GLDAS 2.0 and 2.1, because their anomalies do not match in the years they share.
    • We discarded GLDAS snow (SWE), because the model has no glaciers.
    • We cross-validated every result with independent datasets.
  • Honesty: a dedicated section explains what we can and cannot claim.
  • Accessibility: the app is in Spanish, needs no installation, and works offline.
  • Reproducibility: all data, scripts, and figures are in the repository.
  • Scalability: it can be applied to other regions.
